Was it the bank, or the economy?

We split a bank's share-price risk into three layers: the market, its peer group, and the bank itself. State Bank of India and Federal Bank, FY14 to FY25.

Chapter 1 of 7 · The question

When loans go bad, who is to blame?

When bad loans rise, is it the lender or the economy? Sometimes the whole sector suffers together. Sometimes one lender gets it badly wrong while its peers sail through. We split each bank's price risk into three layers and ask which layer moved, and when.

Market (systematic)Peer group (common to similar banks)Idiosyncratic (the bank alone)

How we split the risk

Layer 1: regress the bank's daily return on the benchmark. Layer 2: add the average return of its peers. What is left is idiosyncratic. The share of variance in each layer is the headline number on every tab.

How data breaks and gaps were handled

Mergers: pre- and post-merger values carry different basis tags and are never joined. Prices: Yahoo adjusted closes; merger share swaps are not adjusted; one missing Nifty Bank day (1 Feb 2025, Budget Saturday session) is left unfilled. PCR is stored on separate bases. Derived values are labelled. Two sources that disagree are listed, not averaged.

Limits

Prices: Yahoo Finance adjusted closes. Credit data: bank filings, with the source on every figure (see Data tab). Work in progress, not investment advice.
